retraction.what_is_retracted: Round 56z claim: 'Adhesion cannot be identified even with perfect sensors' (CE-016 original form)
retraction.why_retracted: CEO correctly identified that naive unknown-count (5 unknowns, ≤4 equations) is insufficient to prove non-identifiability. Time-series observations can provide many equations, and controlled perturbations can make an otherwise underdetermined system identifiable.
retraction.corrected_statement: The current five-component static force model does not establish identifiability. A proper observation/dynamics model with controlled perturbations is required.

ce_016_sharpened.old_form: N unknowns + fewer equations = target cannot be identified
ce_016_sharpened.new_form: Before claiming a latent component is measurable, explicitly formulate the observation/dynamics model and perform an identifiability analysis. A naive unknown-count is INSUFFICIENT — time-series observations can provide many equations, and controlled perturbations can make an otherwise underdetermined system identifiable. Must show rank/observability analysis or construct an explicit non-identifiability counterexample.
ce_016_sharpened.procedure: (1) Define state variables, observables, inputs/perturbations, measurement noise, known/unknown params; (2) Build measurement equations; (3) Test whether Jacobian of observations w.r.t. unknown parameters has full column rank; (4) If not, test whether controlled perturbations can increase rank.

force_model.F_adhesion: a * A_contact(x) * H(threshold - ε) — velocity-INDEPENDENT, constant until adhesion breaks
force_model.F_friction: μ * N_normal(x) * v(t) — LINEAR in velocity
force_model.F_drag: c_d * ρ * A_cross * v(t)² — QUADRATIC in velocity
force_model.F_deformation: k * ε(t) + η * dε/dt — TIME-DEPENDENT (exponential decay at v=0)

controlled_perturbation_identifiability.key_insight: Controlled velocity perturbations can SEPARATE adhesion from velocity-dependent terms.

step_1_relaxation.identifiability: 4 parameters from time-series: a·A·H, k·ε0, η·ε0/τ, τ → IDENTIFIABLE
step_1_relaxation.adhesion_separation: If A is known (imaging) and H=1 (adhesion active): a = (a·A·H) / A → ADHESION IDENTIFIABLE

step_2_velocity_sweep.description: Pull at different velocities v1, v2, v3
step_2_velocity_sweep.what_remains: Friction (linear in v) + drag (quadratic in v) + deformation difference
step_2_velocity_sweep.identifiability: 3 velocities → 2 independent equations → can estimate μ, c_d if ε1≈ε2

step_3_combined.verdict: ALL 5 PARAMETERS STRUCTURALLY IDENTIFIABLE with controlled perturbations

structural_identifiability_verdict.method: Velocity=0 relaxation + multi-velocity sweep + time-series dynamics
key_separations: Multiple velocities separate friction (linear) from drag (quadratic)
Time-series dynamics separate adhesion (constant) from deformation (exponential decay)
structural_identifiability_verdict.previous_kill_RETRACTED: Round 56z kill of Layer A based on naive unknown-count is RETRACTED. Adhesion IS structurally identifiable with controlled perturbations.

practical_identifiability_caveats.structural_vs_practical: Structural identifiability assumes perfect measurements. Practical identifiability is UNCERTAIN.
practical_identifiability_caveats.snr: Can force sensors measure 0.01-0.1 N range? (adhesion force range per literature)
practical_identifiability_caveats.time_scale: Can relaxation be measured before clot re-attaches or embolizes?
practical_identifiability_caveats.clinical_feasibility: Can you stop pulling mid-retrieval? (clinical workflow disruption)
practical_identifiability_caveats.deformation_similarity: Is ε1≈ε2 at different velocities? (may not hold for soft clots)
practical_identifiability_caveats.next_gate: CE-015 (physics authority): can the measurement actually be performed clinically?
